title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: Provide one row per observed subject visit, columns subject ID, numeric time, response, covariates. order x.var determines coefficient labels: beta1 multiplies first covariate, beta2 second, . baseline repeated within subject changing may vary visit. TDMM handles subject indexing spline construction. Gaussian coefficient curves response scale; Bernoulli coefficients log-odds scale Poisson coefficients log-mean scale. Inspect trace plots, R-hat, effective sample size, credible bands interpretation.
code: library(TDMM) fit <- tdmm(long_data, family = "gaussian",             subject.var = "id", time.var = "time", y.var = "y",             x.var = c("baseline", "changing"), n_basis = 8,             control = tdmm_control(chains = 3, iterations = 4000,                                    burn_in = 1500, thin = 2,                                    adapt = 2000, seed = 77181),             priors = tdmm.priors("gaussian")) summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "sigma2.e", "tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: figure illustrates recovery simulated data known coefficient functions. Solid lines show posterior means, dashed lines truth, shaded regions pointwise 95% credible bands. Gaussian example gives fitting code. Bernoulli Poisson examples show workflow binary count outcomes.

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: PBC2 application uses pbc2 dataset JMbayes2: 1,945 observations 312 subjects, 1–16 visits. response log serum bilirubin; predictors baseline treatment indicator longitudinal albumin. Albumin centered overall observation-level mean, 3.3898868894601542 g/dL. Thus intercept represents modeled placebo trajectory albumin level random intercept zero. treatment 95% credible interval includes zero throughout common evaluation grid. albumin coefficient negative, band zero grid. conditional associations, treatment curve establish causal effect. Late follow-sparse, small tail fluctuations read precise clinical changes.

title: Getting Started with TDMM
text: Choose family = "gaussian", "bernoulli", "poisson" supply intended covariates x.var order. data checks reject missing analysis values; decide handle missingness fitting. Varying n_basis useful sensitivity check; scientifically important smoothing variance priors can also examined using tdmm.priors(). independent chains macOS Linux, select parallel execution tdmm_control(parallel = TRUE, cores = 2, ...).

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: TDMM fits Bayesian time-dynamic mixed-effects models longitudinal Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson outcomes. estimates time-varying coefficient functions subject-specific random intercepts. Data may irregular subject-specific observation times, unequal visit counts, baseline covariates, covariates vary visit. default spline uses eight cubic B-spline basis functions (polynomial degree 3, spline order 4) second-order coefficient-difference penalty. JAGS performs posterior sampling.

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: Install JAGS first, install TDMM R:
code: install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM") library(TDMM)

title: Bayesian Time-Dynamic Mixed-Effects Models
text: Supply one row per observed visit. baseline constant within subject changing varies visit: Use family = "bernoulli" binary outcomes family = "poisson" counts. See Getting Started data layout, interpretation, diagnostics. Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson, PBC2 examples give fuller workflows. vignette source example scripts also available repository.
code: fit <- tdmm(long_data, family = "gaussian",             subject.var = "id", time.var = "time", y.var = "y",             x.var = c("baseline", "changing"), n_basis = 8,             control = tdmm_control(chains = 3, seed = 123)) summary(fit) plot(fit) plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "sigma2.e", "tau.alpha[1]"))

title: Fit a time-dynamic mixed-effects model — tdmm
text: Rows may irregular subject-specific times unequal visit counts. Numeric covariates may constant change within subject. Coefficient functions use extended uniform B-spline basis second-order coefficient-difference penalty. default cubic eight basis functions. Use tdmm_control(parallel = TRUE, cores = ...) parallel chains. coefficient functions identity, logit, log link scale Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson responses, respectively.

title: Fit a time-dynamic mixed-effects model — tdmm
text: fitted object class "tdmm" containing posterior samples, reconstructed coefficient functions, input metadata, variance summaries, fitting settings.

title: Fit a time-dynamic mixed-effects model — tdmm
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Requires JAGS and runs MCMC. set.seed(42) my_long_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(20), function(id) {   time <- sort(runif(5))   baseline <- rnorm(1)   changing <- rnorm(5)   data.frame(id = id, time = time, baseline = baseline,              changing = changing,              y = 0.5 + baseline * sin(2*pi*time) +                  changing * (time - 0.5) + rnorm(5, sd = 0.3)) })) fit <- tdmm(my_long_data, family = "gaussian", subject.var = "id",             time.var = "time", y.var = "y", x.var = c("baseline", "changing"),             control = tdmm_control(seed = 42)) summary(fit) plot(fit) } # }

title: Family-specific default TDMM priors — tdmm.priors
text: Gamma distributions use shape rate parameterization. response families, smoothing precision Gamma(1, 0.001) prior. Gaussian outcomes, random-intercept precision residual precision Gamma(1, 0.005) priors. Bernoulli Poisson outcomes, random-intercept standard deviation Uniform(0, 5) prior. Bernoulli outcomes, null_space = list(sd = 10) specifies standard deviation used two unpenalized spline components. Users may modify numerical parameters priors, prior distribution associated response family fixed.

title: TDMM 0.2.0
text: Fit Gaussian, Bernoulli, Poisson longitudinal outcomes subject-specific irregular observation times, unequal visit counts, baseline covariates, time-varying covariates. Use cubic B-splines (degree 3, order 4) second-order coefficient-difference penalty eight basis functions default. n_basis specifies basis dimension directly; older nknots argument remains supported deprecation warning. Fit serial parallel chains tdmm() structured tdmm_control() tdmm.priors() settings. tdmm.parallel() remains compatibility wrapper. Existing Gaussian Poisson model specifications retained.
